Data Privacy Awareness

Pause.
Think.
Verify.

Data privacy means keeping your personal information safe — with the ability to control who can see, use, or share it.

⇄
01 Oversharing +
Posting too much online reveals personal details you didn't mean to share.
Even harmless-looking posts — your birthday, location, workplace, or pet's name — can be pieced together by bad actors to guess passwords, answer security questions, or impersonate you.
02 Phishing +
Fake emails, texts, or websites designed to steal your information.
Phishing attacks disguise themselves as trusted sources — banks, government agencies, or apps you use — to trick you into handing over passwords, credit card numbers, or account access.
03 Weak Passwords +
Easy-to-guess credentials make every account vulnerable.
Using "123456", your name, or the same password across multiple sites is like using one key for everything you own. One breach exposes all of it. Use a password manager.
04 Data Brokers +
Companies that collect and sell your personal profile.
Data brokers aggregate your browsing behavior, purchases, location history, and more — then sell it to advertisers, insurers, or anyone willing to pay, often without your knowledge.
01 — Priority
Use Strong Passwords
Create passwords with a mix of letters, numbers, and symbols. Use a password manager — you only need to remember one master password.
02
Two-Factor Authentication
Adds an extra layer of security. Even if your password is stolen, attackers can't get in without your second factor.
03
Keep Devices Updated
Install security updates regularly. Updates patch vulnerabilities that hackers actively exploit in the wild.
04
Verify Links & Messages
Check if emails and websites are legitimate before clicking. Hover over links to preview the real URL.
05
Review App Permissions
Audit which apps have access to your camera, location, and contacts. Revoke what you don't need.
Identity Theft
When personal data is leaked, it can lead to identity theft — criminals using your information to open credit cards, take out loans, or commit crimes in your name.
Freedom & Autonomy
Privacy preserves your freedom and prevents manipulation. Your data reveals your habits, fears, and desires — which can be exploited to shape your choices without your awareness.
Reputation
Guarded data prevents reputation-damaging deepfakes — fabricated images, videos, or statements made using your likeness that can destroy both your personal and professional life.
The Stakes
The Philippines ranks among the top countries in Southeast Asia affected by phishing attacks. Data breaches affect millions of people every year — and most don't know until it's too late.
